correctness.rationale: For precisely four agents in two identical disutility pairs and three item cost types A=(r,r,r,r), B=(1,1,r,r), C=(r,r,1,1), with arbitrary real r>3, I reconstructed the integer 4×3 allocation incidence matrices and checked that EFX removes an item from the comparing agent’s own bundle while PO quantifies over all allocations. There are C(11,3)=165 profiles with <=8 chores, and 125970 allocation matrices summed over profiles. Every EFX and dominance inequality is affine in r with integer coefficients bounded by eight: the complete sign partition of (3,infinity) has breakpoints 7/2,4,5,6,7,8. I independently implemented exact scaled-integer vectorized enumeration of all 13 representative cells × 165 profiles; every profile has EFX+PO, and for the nine-item (3,3,3) case no EFX+PO occurs in the four independently tested cells. The unrestricted nine-item obstruction is credited to He–Tao Theorem 2, not extrapolated from the four checks. These finite cells are mathematically exhaustive for the positive claim only because all parameter-breakpoint signs were justified.
